virals.text:
The biggest mistake in AI filmmaking? Choosing a tool based on its best-looking demo.

A beautiful 10-second clip doesn't mean you can create a consistent 2-minute film.

Here's what most creators overlook:

AI video generators and AI filmmaking agents solve different problems.

→ A video generator creates individual shots.

→ An AI filmmaking agent helps coordinate the workflow, from planning scenes to generating assets and assembling videos.

But not every agent does everything equally well.

Here's how I'd choose:

→ Script to finished video: invideo, OpenArt, or Frameo.

→ Commercials and brand campaigns: Runway or Luma.

→ Custom production workflows: Krea or Magnific.

Before spending money, test three things:

Can you review the scene plan before generating?

Can you reuse characters and location references across shots?

How many credits will revisions actually cost?

Because generating a great shot is one thing.

Maintaining consistency across 20 shots is a completely different challenge.

The best AI filmmaking agent isn't the one with the most features. It's the one that helps you finish your film with fewer compromises.

.
.
.

virals.draft_en:
Picking an AI filmmaking tool because of its prettiest demo is the most common mistake I see.

A gorgeous 10-second clip says nothing about whether you can make a consistent 2-minute film.

What a lot of creators miss: AI filmmaking agents and AI video generators do different jobs.

- A video generator makes single shots.
- An AI filmmaking agent handles the whole workflow: it plans the scenes, makes the assets and assembles the cut.

And agents are not equally good at everything. Where I'd look:

- Ads and brand work: Luma or Runway
- Going from a script all the way to a final cut: OpenArt, Frameo or invideo
- A production pipeline built your own way: Magnific or Krea

Run three checks before spending a cent:

Do you get to approve the plan for each scene ahead of generation?
Can you reuse character and location references across shots?
What will revisions really cost in credits?

One great shot is easy. Keeping 20 shots consistent is a different job.

The best AI filmmaking agent is not the one with the longest feature list. It is the one that gets your film finished with the fewest compromises.

The biggest mistake in AI filmmaking? Choosing a tool based on its best-looking demo.

A beautiful 10-second clip doesn't mean you can create a consistent 2-minute film.

Here's what most creators overlook:

AI video generators and AI filmmaking agents solve different problems.

→ A video generator creates individual shots.

→ An AI filmmaking agent helps coordinate the workflow, from planning scenes to generating assets and assembling videos.

But not every agent does everything equally well.

Here's how I'd choose:

→ Script to finished video: invideo, OpenArt, or Frameo.

→ Commercials and brand campaigns: Runway or Luma.

→ Custom production workflows: Krea or Magnific.

Before spending money, test three things:

Can you review the scene plan before generating?

Can you reuse characters and location references across shots?

How many credits will revisions actually cost?

Because generating a great shot is one thing.

Maintaining consistency across 20 shots is a completely different challenge.

The best AI filmmaking agent isn't the one with the most features. It's the one that helps you finish your film with fewer compromises.

.
.
.

Picking an AI filmmaking tool because of its prettiest demo is the most common mistake I see.

A gorgeous 10-second clip says nothing about whether you can make a consistent 2-minute film.

What a lot of creators miss: AI filmmaking agents and AI video generators do different jobs.

- A video generator makes single shots.

And agents are not equally good at everything. Where I'd look:

- Ads and brand work: Luma or Runway
- Going from a script all the way to a final cut: OpenArt, Frameo or invideo

Do you get to approve the plan for each scene ahead of generation?
Can you reuse character and location references across shots?
What will revisions really cost in credits?

The best AI filmmaking agent is not the one with the longest feature list. It is the one that gets your film finished with the fewest compromises.
